name: spelling
title: Spanish Spelling Practice: B and V, C, Z, S, H, LL and Y Quiz
description: Practice Spanish spelling: b and v, c, z and s, silent h, ll and y, g and j, qu and gu, and spelling changes in verbs, with a rule table and 10 checked sentences.
answer: Spanish spelling is close to pronunciation, but a few letters share sounds: b and v sound the same, c before e or i, z and s sound alike in Latin America, h is silent, and ll and y sound the same for most speakers. Some sounds need two letters: qu before e and i (queso), gu before e and i (guerra). Verbs change spelling to keep their sound: busqué, llegué, empecé.

rulesCaption: Spanish spelling rules that cause most errors

rules.use: B and V sound the same

rules.meaning: z before a, o, u; c before e, i

rules.use: Hard c and g before e, i

quiz.after: a la playa con mis primos.
quiz.why: Ir is spelled with v: voy.
Hacer has a silent h: hace.
Before e, the hard c sound is written qu: queso.
-gar verbs add u in yo preterite: llegué.

quiz.after: mis llaves por toda la casa.
quiz.why: -car verbs change c to qu in yo preterite: busqué.
Hard g before i: gu, guitarra.
Empezar keeps the z before a: empieza.

mistakes: Mixing b and v by sound: «boy», «baso» and «abía» should be «voy», «vaso» and «había».
Forgetting the silent h: «ablar» and «ora» should be «hablar» and «ahora».
Writing s for z or c: «sapato», «siudad» should be «zapato», «ciudad».
Dropping the u in verb forms: «llegé» and «pagé» should be «llegué» and «pagué».
Writing k for the hard c: «keso» should be «queso»; k appears only in a few borrowed words like kilo.

heritage: Heritage speakers often spell by sound, which leads to b and v, s, c and z, h and y and ll confusions. These are the most frequent errors in heritage writing and also the easiest to fix with reading. Keep a short list of your own frequent words (había, voy, hacer, ciudad) and check them every time.
teacher: Run a mini spelling bee with words from the table: students spell aloud with Spanish letter names (be, uve, ce, zeta, hache) and then write a sentence with each word.

faq.question: Do b and v sound different in Spanish?
faq.answer: No. In modern Spanish, b and v are pronounced the same. The difference exists only in writing, so you learn each word: vaso, bueno, vivir, beber. Related words usually keep the same letter: vivir, vida, vivo.

faq.question: Why do some verbs change spelling in the preterite?
faq.answer: To keep the same sound. Buscar becomes busqué (c would sound like s before e), llegar becomes llegué (g would sound like j) and empezar becomes empecé (Spanish writes ce, not ze).

faq.question: What are the letter names in Spanish?
faq.answer: A, be, ce, de, e, efe, ge, hache, i, jota, ka, ele, eme, ene, eñe, o, pe, cu, erre, ese, te, u, uve, uve doble, equis, ye, zeta. Many Latin Americans say be larga or be grande for b and ve corta or ve chica for v.
